packs.examBy: Your state's licensing agency gives the CDL knowledge and skills tests. The federal rules below are the same in every state; check your state's CDL manual for anything it adds.
packs.blurb: Classes, permits, inspections, hours of service, alcohol, phones, crossings and cargo.

first.title: Who needs a CDL, and which class
body: Class A covers a combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, when the vehicle or vehicles being towed are rated over 10,000 pounds.
Class B covers a single vehicle rated 26,001 pounds or more, or one towing a vehicle rated 10,000 pounds or less.

Class C covers a vehicle or combination that is neither A nor B but is designed to carry 16 or more people counting the driver, or carries hazardous materials in an amount that must be placarded, or any amount of a select agent or toxin.
You may hold only one driver's license at a time. Holding licenses from two states is itself a violation.

A Class A holder may also drive Class B and C vehicles, and a Class B holder may drive Class C vehicles, as long as they hold any endorsement the vehicle needs. Endorsements are needed for double or triple trailers, passenger vehicles, tank vehicles, hazardous materials (a load that must be placarded, or any amount of a select agent or toxin) and school buses. A tank vehicle is one built to haul any liquid or gas in tanks of more than 119 gallons each and 1,000 gallons or more in all.

The skills test vehicle sets restrictions on the license. Test in a vehicle without air brakes and you may not drive one with any type of air brakes; test with air over hydraulic brakes and you may not drive one with full air brakes. Test in an automatic and you may not drive a manual, meaning one with a clutch you work by pedal or lever; any other transmission, semi-automatic included, counts as automatic.

questions.prompt: A tractor with a gross combination weight rating of 40,000 pounds pulls a trailer rated 30,000 pounds. Which class is needed?
questions.why: A combination of 26,001 pounds or more towing a unit rated over 10,000 pounds is Class A.

questions.prompt: A straight truck rated 33,000 pounds tows a trailer rated 8,000 pounds. Which class is needed?
questions.why: A single vehicle of 26,001 pounds or more towing 10,000 pounds or less is Class B.

questions.prompt: A van rated 12,000 pounds is built to carry 16 people including the driver. Which class does it need?
questions.why: A vehicle designed for 16 or more people counting the driver is a commercial vehicle in Class C when it is not A or B.

questions.prompt: How many driver's licenses may a commercial driver hold?
options: One per state where they drive
Two: a CDL and a personal license
questions.why: A driver may hold only one license; holding more than one is a violation.

questions.prompt: How long must you hold a commercial learner's permit before taking the skills test?
questions.why: The skills test may not be taken in the first 14 days after the CLP is first issued.

questions.prompt: With a CLP in a truck, where must the accompanying CDL holder sit?
options: In the front seat beside you
questions.why: In a truck the CDL holder must be in the front seat beside you; in a passenger vehicle they may sit directly behind or in the first row behind the driver.

questions.prompt: A CLP holder has the tank (N) endorsement. What may they drive?
options: A loaded tank vehicle with a trainer
Any tank vehicle once they have 14 days
questions.why: A CLP holder with N may operate only an empty tank vehicle, purged of residue if it held hazardous materials.

questions.prompt: Which endorsements can appear on a commercial learner's permit?
questions.why: A CLP may carry only the passenger, school bus and tank endorsements.

questions.prompt: The last inspection report lists a defect. What must you do before driving?
options: Nothing, if the truck seems safe to you
Sign it, once you see the repair certification
Cross out the defect and drive on
questions.why: You review the last report and sign it to acknowledge the carrier's certification that the defect was repaired or needed no repair.

questions.prompt: You drove a property-carrying truck all day and found no defects. Must you prepare an end-of-day inspection report?
options: No, not when no defect was found or reported
questions.why: No report is required when no defect or deficiency is found by or reported to the driver.

packs.title: CDL Air Brakes
packs.examBy: Your state gives the air brakes knowledge test and checks the air brake inspection in the skills test. Without it, your CDL carries an air brake restriction.
packs.blurb: How the system works, the warning signals, and the in-cab air brake check.
sectionTitles: Gauges and the low air warning
Spring brakes and the parking brake

first.title: How the system works
body: An engine-driven compressor pumps air into storage reservoirs. A governor stops the compressor pumping when the reservoirs reach the cut-out pressure (around 125 psi) and starts it again when pressure falls to the cut-in pressure (around 100 psi).
Pressing the brake pedal sends air to the brake chambers, which push the pushrods, turn the slack adjusters and press the brake shoes against the drums.
Moisture and oil collect in the reservoirs. Every reservoir has a drain valve that can be worked by hand. Manuals say to drain tanks without automatic drains at the end of each working day.
A safety valve, usually set to open at 150 psi, releases air if reservoir pressure climbs too high.

A check valve, or a device that does the same job, must keep the service reservoirs from losing air if something fails between them and the compressor, and you must be able to test it without disconnecting any line. An automatic drain valve is allowed only if it can also be worked by hand or a manual way to drain the tank is kept.

The brake chambers on the two ends of an axle must be the same size, and so must the effective length of the two slack adjusters. Air-braked vehicles built on or after October 20, 1994 must have automatic brake adjusters, and where an external automatic adjuster has an exposed pushrod, a brake adjustment indicator must show when that brake is under-adjusted.

questions.cite: State CDL manual, Air Brakes section
questions.prompt: What tells the compressor to stop pumping air?
questions.why: The governor controls when the compressor pumps: off at cut-out, on again at cut-in.

questions.cite: State CDL manual, Air Brakes section
questions.prompt: Why are air reservoirs drained?
options: To remove water and oil that collect in them
questions.why: Water and oil in the tanks can freeze or damage the brakes.

questions.cite: State CDL manual, Air Brakes section
questions.prompt: What does the slack adjuster do?
options: Turns the brake camshaft when the pushrod moves
questions.why: The pushrod moves the slack adjuster, which turns the brake cam and spreads the shoes.

questions.prompt: Where must the air pressure gauge be?
options: Where the driver can see it from the seat
questions.why: The gauge must be visible to a person seated in the normal driving position.

questions.prompt: On a truck built after 1975, the low air warning must come on when pressure is below:
questions.why: FMVSS 121, applied by 49 CFR 393.51, requires the warning below 60 psi. Some state test sheets use 55 psi or the manufacturer's level.

questions.cite: State CDL manual, Air Brakes section
questions.prompt: What holds spring brakes off?
questions.why: Air holds the springs back; lose the air and the springs apply the brakes.

questions.cite: State CDL manual, Air Brakes section
questions.prompt: As air pressure falls, spring brakes usually come on by themselves between:
questions.why: Manuals give 20 to 45 psi, the same range the federal rule sets for the tractor protection valve.

questions.prompt: A trailer breaks away from the tractor. What must happen to its brakes?
questions.why: Trailer brakes must apply automatically on breakaway.

questions.prompt: An air-braked truck tractor needs antilock brakes if it was built on or after:
questions.why: Tractors from March 1, 1997; other air-braked trucks, buses and trailers from March 1, 1998.

questions.cite: State CDL manual, Air Brakes section
questions.prompt: The antilock malfunction lamp stays on. What still works?
options: Your normal brakes, without the antilock function
questions.why: A fault turns off the antilock function; normal braking remains.

packs.title: Combination Vehicles
packs.examBy: Your state's licensing agency gives the combination vehicles knowledge test, and the Class A skills test that follows it. Check your state's CDL manual for how it runs both.
packs.blurb: Class A: trailer air, the tractor protection valve, coupling and uncoupling, inspection and rollover.

Coupling a tractor to a semitrailer

first.title: What Class A is and what the test covers
body: Class A (Group A in the federal rule) is any combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, when the vehicle or vehicles being towed are rated over 10,000 pounds. A single vehicle rated 26,001 pounds or more that tows a trailer rated 10,000 pounds or less is Class B.

Every driver who runs combination vehicles must know three areas on top of the general knowledge: how to couple and uncouple a tractor and semitrailer; the inspection steps that are unique to combinations; and how to operate a combination safely, including its air brakes. Your state checks these in the combination vehicles knowledge test.

The skills test is taken in a vehicle that fits the group. If you test in a tractor trailer, you must be able to explain its special features during the pre-trip inspection, and, with air brakes, show that the air connections between the vehicles are properly made and secured.
Pass the Class A knowledge and skills tests and you may also drive Class B and Class C vehicles, as long as you hold any endorsement those need.
Class A is a class, not an endorsement: a single tractor and semitrailer needs no endorsement. Pulling doubles or triples does need the T endorsement.

The vehicle you test in matters. Test in a truck and trailer joined by a pintle hook or other connection that is not a fifth wheel, and your CDL is restricted from tractor-trailers coupled by a fifth wheel. Test in a vehicle without air brakes, or fail the air brake part of the knowledge test, and you get the air brake restriction.

questions.prompt: A combination has a gross combination weight rating of 34,000 pounds. For it to need Class A, the towed unit must be rated:
questions.why: Group A needs a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more with the towed vehicle or vehicles rated over 10,000 pounds.

questions.prompt: You take the Class A pre-trip inspection test in a tractor-trailer. Besides the parts every vehicle has, what must you be able to explain?
options: The trailer's bill of lading and the load's weight
The special features of a tractor trailer
questions.why: The pre-trip skills list adds the special features of a tractor trailer when one is the test vehicle.

questions.prompt: Which is one of the three knowledge areas the federal rule adds for combination vehicle drivers?
options: Coupling and uncoupling a tractor and semitrailer
Loading and unloading passengers at stops and terminals
questions.why: The combination areas are coupling and uncoupling, inspection unique to combinations, and safe operation including air brakes.

questions.prompt: You pass the Class A skills test in an air-braked tractor-trailer, but you failed the air brake part of the knowledge test. What goes on your CDL?
options: Nothing, the skills test outweighs it
A restriction from driving any vehicle with air brakes
A restriction from pulling doubles and triples until you retest
questions.why: Failing the air brake part of the knowledge test brings the air brake restriction, whatever vehicle the skills test was taken in.

questions.prompt: You take the Class A skills test in a truck and trailer joined by a pintle hook. What restriction goes on your CDL?
options: No tractor-trailers coupled by a fifth wheel
questions.why: Testing with a pintle hook or other non-fifth-wheel connection restricts you from fifth-wheel tractor-trailers that need Class A.

questions.prompt: Which endorsement does a single tractor and semitrailer need on a Class A CDL?
questions.why: Endorsements are listed for doubles and triples, passengers, tanks, hazardous materials and school buses, not for a single trailer.

questions.prompt: In an air-braked Class A skills test, what must you show about the connections between tractor and trailer?
options: That the glad hands are less than a year old and unpainted
That the air connections are properly made and secured
That the lines are colored red and blue
questions.why: The skills rule requires you to determine that air system connections between the vehicles have been properly made and secured.

questions.prompt: Under the federal definitions, what makes a trailer a semitrailer?
options: It is shorter than 28 feet from its nose to its rear doors
It has no brakes of its own
Some of its weight rests on the towing vehicle
questions.why: A semitrailer is built so that some part of its weight rests on the vehicle towing it.

questions.prompt: What must a fifth wheel's locking mechanism do?
options: Keep the halves together until a positive manual release is worked
Release by itself once the tractor comes to a stop
Lock only when the trailer is loaded
questions.why: The lock must prevent separation of the upper and lower halves unless a positive manual release is activated.

questions.prompt: May the fifth wheel release be placed so you can work it from the cab?
options: No, it must be worked at the fifth wheel
questions.why: The rule says the release may be located so the driver can operate it from the cab.

packs.title: HazMat Endorsement and DOT Hazmat Training
packs.examBy: Your state's licensing agency gives the H endorsement knowledge test, and TSA runs the security threat assessment. DOT hazmat employee training is given and recorded by your employer. The federal rules below are the same in every state; check your state's CDL manual for anything it adds.
packs.blurb: Classes, shipping papers, placards, crossings, parking, routes, emergencies and the hazmat training rule.
sectionTitles: Shipping papers and where they ride

DOT hazmat employee training (49 CFR 172 Subpart H)
Reference: the hazard classes and divisions

first.title: Who needs the H endorsement
body: You need the hazardous materials (H) endorsement to drive a commercial motor vehicle that must be placarded for hazardous materials under 49 CFR 172 Subpart F, or that carries any quantity of a select agent or toxin listed in 42 CFR part 73.
A vehicle too light for Class A or B still needs a Class C CDL when it carries hazardous materials that must be placarded, or any quantity of a select agent or toxin.

The H knowledge test checks that you know the hazardous materials rules well enough to follow them: recognizing hazardous materials, shipping papers, marking, labeling and placarding, handling and loading, emergency equipment, and what to do in an emergency.

The endorsement is in addition to your CDL class. Hazmat rules for drivers also sit in the motor carrier rules: railroad crossings (49 CFR 392.10), the fire extinguisher (49 CFR 393.95) and driving and parking (49 CFR 397).

The H endorsement takes a knowledge test only; there is no H skills test. It cannot be placed on a commercial learner's permit, and a CLP holder may not drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials as 49 CFR 383.5 defines them, even with a CDL holder in the next seat.

questions.prompt: Which commercial vehicles need a driver with the H endorsement?
options: Any tank vehicle, loaded or empty
Any vehicle of 26,001 pounds or more
questions.why: The H endorsement is required for a vehicle that must be placarded, or that carries a select agent or toxin.

questions.prompt: A 14,000 pound truck must be placarded for its load. Which CDL class covers it?
questions.why: A vehicle that is neither A nor B is Class C when it carries hazardous materials that must be placarded.

questions.prompt: Which cargo needs the H endorsement in any quantity, placarded or not?
questions.why: For the CDL rules, hazardous materials include any quantity of a listed select agent or toxin.

questions.prompt: What does the H endorsement knowledge test cover?
options: The rules, handling, equipment and response
questions.why: The test checks knowledge of the hazardous materials rules and how to handle and respond to hazardous materials.

questions.prompt: What must happen before a state may issue or renew an H endorsement?
options: TSA determines the driver is not a security threat
The driver passes a second road test
The carrier signs a letter for the driver
questions.why: The state may not issue, renew, upgrade or transfer the H without TSA's determination, or a valid TWIC, which rests on the same TSA assessment.

questions.prompt: Which is part of TSA's security threat assessment?
options: A check for disqualifying criminal offences
questions.why: TSA looks at criminal offences, immigration status, mental capacity and intelligence records.

questions.prompt: What is a Class 3 material?
questions.why: Class 3 is flammable liquids.

questions.prompt: A flammable liquid has a flash point of not more than:
questions.why: Not more than 60°C (140°F) is a flammable liquid.

questions.prompt: A liquid has a flash point of 75°C. What is it?
questions.why: Above 60°C and below 93°C is a combustible liquid.

questions.prompt: What is Division 2.3?
questions.why: 2.1 is flammable, 2.2 non-flammable and non-poisonous, 2.3 poisonous by inhalation.

packs.title: Passenger (P) Endorsement
packs.examBy: Your state's licensing agency gives the P endorsement knowledge test and the skills test in a passenger vehicle. The federal rules below are the same in every state; check your state's CDL manual for anything it adds.
packs.blurb: Who needs P, passenger hours of service, crossings, standees, baggage and emergencies.
sectionTitles: Hours of service for passenger carriers

first.title: Who needs the P endorsement
body: A vehicle designed to transport 16 or more people, counting the driver, is a commercial motor vehicle for CDL purposes even when it is too light for Class A or B. That smaller vehicle is Group C.

To drive a passenger vehicle that needs a CDL you also need the passenger endorsement, shown on the license as P. It takes a knowledge test and a skills test, and the skills test is taken in a passenger vehicle of the group you will drive.
The state can restrict the endorsement by class: restriction M means no Class A passenger vehicle, and restriction N means no Class A or B passenger vehicle.
A learner's permit may carry P once you pass the P knowledge test, but you may carry no passengers except auditors and inspectors, test examiners, other trainees and the CDL holder training you.
The school bus endorsement (S) builds on P: an S applicant must also pass the P knowledge and skills tests. P, S and N (tank vehicle) are the only endorsements a learner's permit may carry.

Passing the tests for a bigger group covers the smaller ones. Group A lets you drive Group B and C vehicles, and Group B lets you drive any Group C vehicle, as long as you hold the endorsements that vehicle needs.

questions.prompt: A van is rated 9,000 pounds and designed to seat 16 people counting the driver. Is it a commercial motor vehicle for CDL purposes?
options: Yes, as Group C, by its design
Only if it carries paying passengers
questions.why: A vehicle designed to transport 16 or more including the driver falls in Group C even when it is light.

questions.prompt: Which tests does the P endorsement require?
options: A knowledge test and a skills test
questions.why: Passenger and school bus endorsements each need a knowledge test and a skills test.

questions.prompt: What vehicle is the P skills test taken in?
options: Any vehicle in the class you hold
A passenger vehicle of the group you will drive
A Group C vehicle, passenger or not
questions.why: The skills test is taken in a passenger vehicle meeting the requirements of that vehicle group.

questions.prompt: You hold a learner's permit with P. Who may ride on the bus while you practise?
options: Anyone, so long as the trainer is aboard
Only inspectors, examiners, trainees and your trainer
Up to 15 passengers, with the trainer aboard
questions.why: A CLP holder with P may carry no passengers other than those listed in the rule.

questions.prompt: A CDL shows restriction M. What does it mean for passenger vehicles?
options: No passenger vehicle of any class
questions.why: M means no Class A passenger vehicle; N means no Class A or B passenger vehicle.

questions.prompt: After 8 consecutive hours off duty, how many hours may a bus driver drive?
questions.why: Passenger-carrying drivers may drive no more than 10 hours following 8 consecutive hours off duty.

questions.prompt: After how many hours on duty may a bus driver no longer drive, following 8 hours off duty?
questions.why: No driving after being on duty 15 hours following 8 consecutive hours off duty.

questions.prompt: How long must a bus driver be off duty, consecutively, before the 10 and 15 hour limits start over?
questions.why: The passenger limits run from 8 consecutive hours off duty, not the 10 hours in the truck rule.

questions.prompt: Your carrier runs buses every day of the week. What is your weekly on-duty limit?
questions.why: 70 hours in 8 consecutive days when the carrier operates every day; otherwise 60 in 7.

questions.prompt: A motorcoach driver splits sleeper berth time into two periods. What is the shortest either period may be?
questions.why: Neither sleeper period may be shorter than 2 hours.

packs.title: School Bus (S) Endorsement
packs.examBy: Your state's licensing agency gives the S endorsement knowledge and skills tests, and your state's law sets the rules for stops, lights and loading. Learn your state's CDL manual and school bus laws alongside this.
packs.blurb: What S requires, which federal rules reach a school bus, the equipment standards, and what your state sets.
sectionTitles: Which federal rules reach a school bus

first.title: What the S endorsement takes
body: You must first qualify for the passenger endorsement: pass the P knowledge and skills tests.

Then the S knowledge test covers loading and unloading children, including the stop signal devices, external mirror systems, flashing lights and other safety devices that state or federal law requires on school buses; emergency exits and evacuating passengers; the state and federal laws for railroad crossings; and other operating practices.
The S skills test is taken in a school bus of the same vehicle group as the bus you will drive.
A learner's permit may carry S once you pass the S knowledge test, but the bus may carry no passengers except auditors and inspectors, test examiners, other trainees and the CDL holder training you.
Passenger, school bus and tank vehicle are the only endorsements a learner's permit may carry.
While you train on a permit, the CDL holder supervising you must ride directly behind you or in the first row behind you, watching you drive.

questions.prompt: What must you hold or qualify for before you can get the S endorsement?
questions.why: An S applicant must pass the knowledge and skills tests for the passenger endorsement.

questions.prompt: Which tests does the S endorsement require?
options: A knowledge test and a skills test
questions.why: School bus, like passenger, takes both a knowledge and a skills test.

questions.prompt: What vehicle is the S skills test taken in?
options: Any bus of the same vehicle group
A school bus of the same vehicle group
A passenger van of any group
questions.why: The skills test is in a school bus of the same vehicle group as the one you will drive.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a topic on the S knowledge test?
options: External mirror systems and stop signal devices
questions.why: Loading and unloading children, including stop signal devices, mirrors and flashing lights, is a listed topic.

questions.prompt: Which is also on the S knowledge test?
questions.why: Emergency exits and procedures for safely evacuating passengers are a listed topic.

questions.prompt: You hold a learner's permit with S. May you drive a route with students aboard if your trainer sits behind you?
options: Yes, on a morning route only
questions.why: A CLP holder with S may carry only auditors and inspectors, test examiners, other trainees and the trainer; no students.

questions.prompt: Under the CDL rules, which trip counts as school bus use?
options: A charter company's tour for a senior club
Teachers to a conference on a for-hire coach
questions.why: The CDL definition covers home to school, school to home, and school-sponsored events, but not for-hire carrier operations.

questions.prompt: In the safety rules, a school bus is designed or used to carry how many passengers?
options: More than 10 in addition to the driver
questions.why: More than 10 passengers in addition to the driver.

questions.prompt: School bus operations are excepted from most of parts 390 to 399. Which rule still applies?
options: The ban on hand-held phones and texting while driving
questions.why: The exception keeps 392.80 and 392.82 (texting and phones), 391.15(e) and (f), and 392.15.

questions.prompt: Does federal drug and alcohol testing apply to school bus drivers who need a CDL?
options: Yes, the part 390 exceptions do not reach the testing rule
questions.why: Part 382 covers every CDL driver and says the 390.3T exceptions do not apply to it.

packs.title: Tank Vehicle (N) Endorsement
packs.examBy: Your state's licensing agency gives the N endorsement knowledge test. The federal rules below are the same in every state; check your state's CDL manual for anything it adds.
packs.blurb: What counts as a tank vehicle, surge, baffles, braking, crossings and attending a cargo tank.
sectionTitles: What counts as a tank vehicle
Crossings and attending a cargo tank

first.title: What counts as a tank vehicle
body: A tank vehicle is a commercial motor vehicle designed to carry liquid or gas in a tank or tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, attached permanently or temporarily to the vehicle or chassis.
An empty storage tank that is not designed for transportation, rated 1,000 gallons or more and temporarily attached to a flatbed trailer, is not a tank vehicle.
The N endorsement needs a knowledge test only, no skills test. A driver with both N and the hazardous materials endorsement may have them shown together as X.
A learner's permit may carry N once you pass the N knowledge test, but you may drive only an empty tank vehicle, and never one that held hazardous materials unless it has been purged of all residue.
Only three endorsements may go on a commercial learner's permit: passenger (P), school bus (S) and tank vehicle (N).

questions.prompt: Which of these is a tank vehicle?
questions.why: Each tank is over 119 gallons and together they hold 1,000 gallons or more.

questions.prompt: What is the aggregate rated capacity that makes a tank vehicle?
questions.why: 1,000 gallons or more in total, in tanks each over 119 gallons.

questions.prompt: An individual tank must be larger than what capacity to count toward a tank vehicle?
questions.why: Each tank counts when its rated capacity is more than 119 gallons.

questions.prompt: You haul an empty 2,000-gallon storage tank, not built for transport, strapped to a flatbed. Is that a tank vehicle?
options: Only if it once held fuel
questions.why: An empty storage container tank not designed for transportation, temporarily attached to a flatbed, is not a tank vehicle.

questions.prompt: Which tests does the N endorsement require?
options: A knowledge and a skills test
questions.why: Tank vehicle is a knowledge test only.

questions.prompt: What letter shows tank vehicle and hazardous materials endorsements together?
questions.why: X is the code for the combination of tank vehicle and hazardous materials.

questions.prompt: A learner's permit holder with N may drive which tank vehicle?
options: A full tank, with a trainer aboard
Only an empty one, purged if it held hazmat
Any tank under 3,000 gallons, empty or not
questions.why: A CLP with N allows only an empty tank, and not one with hazardous materials residue.

questions.prompt: You brake hard with a half-full tank. What does the liquid do?
options: Surges forward and pushes the truck ahead
questions.why: Liquid keeps moving when the truck slows, so it runs forward and pushes.

questions.prompt: What do baffles control best?
questions.why: Baffles slow front-to-back flow; they do little against side-to-side movement.

questions.prompt: Which tank surges hardest?
options: A smooth bore tank with no baffles
questions.why: With nothing inside to slow it, liquid in an unbaffled tank surges the most.

packs.title: Doubles and Triples (T) Endorsement
packs.examBy: Your state's licensing agency gives the T endorsement knowledge test. Whether triples may run at all is set by each state; check your state's CDL manual and size and weight rules.
packs.blurb: Coupling, the converter dolly, breakaway brakes, rearward sway, rollover and sharing the road.
sectionTitles: Converter dollies, safety chains and air

first.title: What the T endorsement covers
body: Pulling double or triple trailers needs the T endorsement. It takes a knowledge test only, no skills test.

The test must cover how the units are assembled and hooked up; where the heaviest trailer goes; handling and stability, including off-tracking, response to steering, braking, oscillatory sway, rollover in steady turns and yaw stability; and the problems a long combination makes for other drivers, such as slow climbing on grades, long passing times, blocking freeway entrances, splash and spray, buffeting, blocked views and lane position.
A learner's permit may not carry the T endorsement; only P, S and N are allowed on a permit.
The endorsement is issued by your state, and only to a driver who passes its test.

questions.prompt: Which tests does the T endorsement require?
options: A knowledge and a skills test
questions.why: Double/triple trailers is a knowledge test only.

questions.prompt: Can a learner's permit carry the T endorsement?
questions.why: The only endorsements allowed on a CLP are P, S and N.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a topic the T test must cover?
questions.why: Handling and stability, including oscillatory sway, is listed.

questions.prompt: A semitrailer sits on a converter dolly behind the first trailer. What is it under the rules?
questions.why: A semitrailer with a converter dolly is considered a full trailer.

questions.prompt: Why must a converter dolly have safety chains or cables?
options: To hold up the air lines and glad hands
To hold the trailer if the tow-bar fails
To help steer the dolly in turns
questions.why: The safety device keeps the towed unit attached if the tow-bar fails or disconnects.

questions.prompt: Where may the safety chains not be attached?
options: To the frame of the towing trailer
To the pintle hook that holds the tow-bar
questions.why: The safety device must not be attached to the pintle hook or other device the tow-bar uses.

questions.prompt: How strong must the safety chains and their attachments be?
options: At least half the towed weight
At least the full towed weight
At least twice the dolly's weight
questions.why: Their ultimate strength must be at least the gross weight of the vehicle or vehicles towed.

questions.prompt: A trailer breaks away from the combination. What must its brakes do?
questions.why: Trailers that must have brakes must have them apply automatically and immediately on breakaway.

questions.prompt: Between what pressures must the tractor protection valve close automatically?
questions.why: Between 20 psi and 45 psi.

questions.prompt: On a set of doubles, how should the rear air shut-off valves be set?
options: Open, except at the very back
questions.why: Air must reach every trailer's brakes (393.48), so state manuals have the valves open at the back of the first trailer and closed at the back of the last.

packs.title: TWIC Card
packs.examBy: There is no TWIC exam. TSA decides each application through its security threat assessment; this pack explains the rules it applies so you know where you stand before you enroll.
packs.blurb: Who needs a TWIC, how enrollment and the threat assessment work, disqualifying offenses, waivers and validity.
sectionTitles: Appeals, waivers and how long it lasts

first.title: Who needs a TWIC
body: The Transportation Worker Identification Credential is required for anyone who needs unescorted access to the secure areas of vessels, port facilities and outer continental shelf facilities regulated under the maritime security rules (33 CFR parts 104, 105 and 106). Truck drivers who pick up and deliver inside a port terminal's secure area are among those who need one.

Federal officials use their own agency credential instead. State and local law enforcement do not need one, and state and local emergency responders do not need one during an emergency; either may get one voluntarily.

A TWIC is not a hazardous materials endorsement: the HME is added by your state after its knowledge test. The two rest on the same TSA threat assessment standard, and each can stand in for the other's assessment. A state may issue, renew, upgrade or transfer an HME to a driver who holds a valid TWIC. Going the other way, TSA treats a current HME threat assessment as comparable for a TWIC: an HME holder still enrolls for the card, and that TWIC expires five years from the date tied to the HME assessment.

If you do not hold a TWIC and are not exempt, you may still enter a secure area under escort. Only a TWIC holder who is authorized to be in that secure area under the facility security plan may serve as the escort, and the escort must accompany you continuously, side by side or by monitoring, closely enough to see whether you are doing anything other than what you were let in for.

You must also show personal identification that resists tampering and shows your full name, a photo that looks like you now, and the name of the issuer. The issuer may be a government authority, or your employer, union or trade association.

questions.prompt: Who must hold a TWIC?
options: Anyone needing unescorted access to secure maritime areas
Anyone who drives across a state line
questions.why: The TWIC is the credential for unescorted access to secure areas under 33 CFR parts 104 to 106.

questions.prompt: A city police officer needs to enter a port's secure area. Is a TWIC required?
questions.why: State and local law enforcement are not required to obtain a TWIC, though they may.

questions.prompt: Does a TWIC give you the hazardous materials endorsement on your CDL?
options: No, it is a separate credential
questions.why: Your state adds the HME after its knowledge test; a valid TWIC can satisfy the TSA threat assessment the state needs for it.

questions.prompt: Which is part of the TWIC security threat assessment?
questions.why: It includes a fingerprint-based criminal history records check, an intelligence-related check and a final disposition.

questions.prompt: TSA serves you an Initial Determination of Threat Assessment. How long do you have to appeal or ask for more time before it becomes final?
questions.why: If you do not appeal or request an extension within 60 days, it becomes final.

questions.why: Murder is a permanent disqualifying offense; robbery and bribery are interim offenses.

questions.why: Within 7 years of the application, or released from incarceration within 5 years.

options: No, the conviction is over 7 years old
Yes, release from incarceration within 5 years counts
questions.why: An interim offense also disqualifies when release from incarceration was within 5 years of applying.

questions.prompt: Which does not count as a dishonesty or fraud offense for TWIC?
options: Money laundering tied to a listed crime
questions.why: Welfare fraud and passing bad checks are excluded.

packs.title: Federal Fleet Driving
packs.examBy: There is no federal fleet driving exam. Your agency authorizes who drives its vehicles and may add its own training; this pack covers the government-wide rules in the Federal Management Regulation.
packs.blurb: What a Government motor vehicle is, permitted use, home-to-work rules, misuse, markings and plates.

first.title: What the rule covers
body: The part governs motor vehicles the Government owns, leases commercially, or leases through GSA Fleet. Executive agencies must follow all of it, and its home-to-work section also reaches employees of the judicial and legislative branches, except the Senate, the House, the Architect of the Capitol and the District of Columbia government.
A Government motor vehicle is any motor vehicle the Government owns or leases, including vehicles obtained by purchase, excess, forfeiture, commercial lease or GSA Fleet lease.

Not covered: military design vehicles, vehicles used for field training, combat or tactical purposes, vehicles used mainly inside a military post, camp or depot, and investigative, law enforcement or intelligence vehicles under the exclusive control the agency head finds essential. Those last are still bound by the use rules in the part's subpart D, except the home-to-work section, and by its subpart J.
A commercial lease is 120 continuous days or more from a commercial source. Anything shorter is a rental.

A Government-owned motor vehicle is one the Government holds title to, whether it came by purchase, excess, forfeiture or some other way. A commercially leased vehicle is still a Government motor vehicle, but the Government does not hold its title, so it is not Government-owned.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a Government motor vehicle?
options: Only a vehicle the Government holds title to
Any it owns or leases, GSA Fleet included
Any vehicle an employee drives while on duty
questions.why: It includes vehicles obtained by purchase, excess, forfeiture, commercial lease or GSA Fleet lease.

questions.why: Less than 120 continuous days from a commercial source is a rental; 120 or more is a commercial lease.

questions.why: Military design vehicles and those used for combat or tactical purposes are not covered.

options: Anything while you are on the clock
Your agency's missions, as it authorizes
Any trip under 50 miles, on duty or not

questions.prompt: May you drive the agency car home each night because the bus is slow?
options: Yes, if your supervisor agrees in writing
questions.why: Home-to-work needs an agency head determination for a listed reason; convenience is not one.

questions.why: The agency head may not delegate the authority to make home-to-work determinations.

questions.prompt: How long can a first home-to-work determination for field work last?
questions.why: Initial determinations for field work last no longer than two years; for other reasons, fifteen days.

questions.why: Field work, clear and present danger, emergency, or a compelling operational consideration.

questions.why: The section does not apply to home-to-work use in conjunction with TDY or relocation.

questions.why: A written agency head determination valid for one year.

packs.examBy: Chauffeur, livery and for-hire licenses are issued by your state and often by your city or airport, each with its own test or none. This pack covers the federal rules that apply on top of them; ask your state licensing agency and local livery authority for theirs.

first.title: When a passenger vehicle is a commercial motor vehicle
body: Under the federal safety rules, a vehicle used on a highway in interstate commerce is a commercial motor vehicle if it is designed or used to carry more than 8 passengers, counting the driver, for compensation, or more than 15 passengers, counting the driver, not for compensation. Weight also counts: 10,001 pounds or more makes it one regardless of seats.

So a for-hire stretch limousine or van seating 9 or more, counting you, on an interstate trip, is a commercial motor vehicle and the federal carrier rules apply. A sedan or SUV built for 8 or fewer, counting you, and carrying no more, is not, unless it is heavy enough.
The rules' definition of a bus covers any motor vehicle designed, built or used to carry passengers, including taxicabs.
Trips that stay within one state are regulated by that state, which may or may not adopt the federal rules.

The definition says designed or used. A vehicle built for fewer seats still counts once it is used to carry more than 8 people, counting the driver, for compensation. A trip between two places in one state is interstate commerce if the route passes through another state.

Charter transportation means a group with a common purpose that hires the whole vehicle under one contract at a fixed charge for the vehicle, for its exclusive use, on a route set in advance or changed along the way.

questions.prompt: A for-hire limousine is designed to carry 10 people counting the driver and makes an interstate trip. Is it a commercial motor vehicle under the safety rules?
options: Yes, it carries over 8 for hire
Only if it weighs over 26,000 pounds
questions.why: More than 8 passengers, including the driver, for compensation makes it a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.prompt: What is the passenger threshold for a vehicle not used for compensation?
options: 16 or more not counting the driver
questions.why: More than 15 passengers, including the driver, when not used to transport passengers for compensation.

questions.prompt: Does the federal definition of a bus include a taxicab?
questions.why: Bus means any motor vehicle designed, built or used to carry passengers, including taxicabs.

questions.prompt: Which weight alone makes a vehicle a commercial motor vehicle under the safety rules, in interstate commerce?
questions.why: A rating or weight of 10,001 pounds or more, whichever is greater.

questions.prompt: Your limo runs only within one state. Whose rules govern it?
options: No one's, if it stays local
questions.why: The federal definition covers vehicles used in interstate commerce; intrastate work is the state's to regulate.

questions.prompt: A limousine seats 12 counting the driver and weighs 9,000 pounds. Does the driver need a CDL under the federal rule?
questions.why: The CDL threshold for a light passenger vehicle is Group C: designed for 16 or more including the driver.

questions.prompt: A party bus is designed for 20 people counting the driver and weighs 14,000 pounds. Which CDL group is it?
questions.why: Under 26,001 pounds but designed for 16 or more: Group C.

questions.prompt: What else does that party bus driver need on the CDL?
questions.why: Driving a passenger vehicle that needs a CDL takes the P endorsement.

questions.prompt: A church van weighs 8,000 pounds, seats 12 counting the driver and is not used for direct compensation. Which federal rule still applies?
options: The ban on texting and hand-held phones
questions.why: The 9 to 15 passenger exception keeps the texting and phone bans and their disqualifications.

questions.prompt: A van carries 12 workers on one daily round trip to and from their jobs. Does the federal passenger carrier financial responsibility rule reach it?
options: No, a commute trip for fewer than 16 is excepted
Only if it crosses two state lines
questions.why: 387.27 excepts a vehicle carrying fewer than 16 people in a single daily round trip to commute to and from work.

packs.examBy: The FAA gives the Remote Pilot knowledge test at a testing center the FAA authorizes. This pack covers the operating rules in 14 CFR 107; the test also asks about charts, weather and aircraft performance, which the FAA's own study guide covers.

first.title: Who needs a remote pilot certificate
body: Part 107 covers small unmanned aircraft, which means under 55 pounds at takeoff including everything on board or attached.

Anyone flying under Part 107, which includes any flight that is not purely recreational, must hold a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating, or fly under the direct supervision of someone who does and who can take over the controls at once.

To get the certificate you must be at least 16, able to read, speak, write and understand English, in a physical and mental condition to fly safely, and pass the initial knowledge test (a Part 61 pilot certificate holder, other than a student pilot, who is current on the flight review may complete the FAA's online training instead).
To keep flying, you must have passed the initial test or completed recurrent training within the previous 24 calendar months.
Flying only for fun falls under a separate law, 49 U.S.C. 44809, with its own conditions. This pack is about Part 107.
If you fail the knowledge test, you must wait 14 calendar days before you may take it again.

questions.prompt: What is the most a small unmanned aircraft may weigh at takeoff under Part 107?
options: Less than 55 pounds, everything on board included
Less than 55 pounds, payload not counted
questions.why: Under 55 pounds at takeoff, including everything on board or otherwise attached.

questions.prompt: How old must you be to hold a remote pilot certificate?
questions.why: At least 16 years old.

questions.prompt: How often must a remote pilot complete recurrent training to keep flying under Part 107?
questions.why: Within the previous 24 calendar months.

questions.prompt: What is the highest you may normally fly?
questions.why: 400 feet above ground level, unless within 400 feet of a structure.

questions.prompt: You are inspecting a 300-foot tower. How high may you fly while within 400 feet of it?
options: No higher than the top of the tower
questions.why: Up to 400 feet above the structure's top: 300 plus 400 is 700 feet above ground level.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum groundspeed?
questions.why: 87 knots, which is 100 miles per hour.

questions.prompt: What is the least flight visibility allowed from the control station?
questions.why: At least 3 statute miles.

questions.prompt: How far below a cloud must the aircraft stay?
questions.why: At least 500 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontally from, clouds.

questions.prompt: How far horizontally from a cloud must the aircraft stay?
questions.why: 2,000 feet horizontally.

questions.prompt: Which of these keeps a flight within visual line of sight?
options: Watching the live camera feed on the controller
A visual observer watching it with unaided eyes
questions.why: Line of sight means unaided eyes (corrective lenses allowed) of the pilot in command, the person at the controls, or a visual observer.

packs.examBy: The FAA gives the Private Pilot knowledge test at a testing center the FAA authorizes. This pack covers the rules in 14 CFR 61 and 91, airspace and VFR weather minimums; the test also asks about aerodynamics, performance, charts, weather theory and navigation, which the FAA's own handbooks (the Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, the Airplane Flying Handbook and the AIM) cover.

first.title: Getting the certificate
body: A student pilot certificate needs you to be at least 16 (14 for a glider or balloon) and able to read, speak, write and understand English.

For a private pilot certificate with an airplane rating you must be at least 17, meet the same English requirement, hold a student, sport or recreational pilot certificate, have an instructor's endorsement before the knowledge test, pass the knowledge test, have an instructor's endorsement before the practical test, meet the aeronautical experience, and pass the practical test.

The knowledge test must have been passed within the 24 calendar months before the month you complete the practical test. The only relief from that for a private pilot applicant is narrow: 61.40 lets a person who served outside the United States in support of U.S. Armed Forces operations use an expired test report, if the practical test is completed within 6 calendar months after returning.

Aeronautical experience for a single-engine airplane: at least 40 hours of flight time, including at least 20 hours of flight training from an authorized instructor and 10 hours of solo flight training. Up to 2.5 hours of instructor training in a flight simulator or flight training device may count, and a private pilot course at a Part 142 training center can lower the total to 35 hours.

The training must include 3 hours of cross-country training; 3 hours of night training with one cross-country flight of over 100 nautical miles total distance and 10 takeoffs and 10 landings to a full stop (a person trained in and living in Alaska may instead get a certificate marked "Night flying prohibited" and must finish the night training within 12 calendar months); 3 hours of flight by reference to instruments; and 3 hours of training in preparation for the practical test within the 2 calendar months before the month of the test.

The 10 hours of solo must include 5 hours of solo cross-country time; one solo cross-country of 150 nautical miles total distance, with full-stop landings at three points and one leg of more than 50 nautical miles straight-line distance; and three takeoffs and three landings to a full stop at an airport with an operating control tower.

questions.prompt: How old must you be to hold a private pilot certificate with an airplane rating?
questions.why: At least 17 for a rating other than glider or balloon.

questions.prompt: Outside a Part 142 training center course, what is the least total flight time for a private pilot certificate, single-engine airplane?
questions.why: At least 40 hours, including 20 hours of training from an instructor and 10 hours of solo training; a Part 142 training center course can lower it to 35.

150 nm total, landings at two points, one leg over 50 nm
150 nm total, landings at three points, one leg over 50 nm
questions.why: 150 nautical miles total, full-stop landings at three points, and one straight-line leg of more than 50 nautical miles.

questions.prompt: How long is a passed knowledge test good for when you take the practical test?
questions.why: It must be passed within the 24 calendar months before the month you complete the practical test; 61.40 gives narrow relief only to people serving abroad in support of the Armed Forces.

questions.prompt: You were 35 when you took your third-class medical exam. How long does it last for private pilot privileges?
questions.why: Under 40 on the exam date, it runs to the end of the 60th month after the month of the exam.

questions.prompt: You were 52 when you took your third-class medical exam. How long does it last for private pilot privileges?
questions.why: At 40 or older on the exam date, it runs to the end of the 24th month after the month of the exam.

questions.prompt: Under BasicMed, how often do you need the comprehensive exam by a State-licensed physician?
questions.why: The comprehensive exam is within the previous 48 calendar months; the education course is within 24.

questions.prompt: Which flight is outside BasicMed limits?
questions.why: BasicMed flights may not go above 18,000 feet MSL, faster than 250 knots, or carry more than 6 passengers.

questions.prompt: You fly two friends to the coast. How may the costs be shared?
options: They may pay all of the fuel and rental
You pay at least your pro rata share of the fuel and rental
They pay your share if you add a fee for your time
questions.why: A private pilot may not pay less than the pro rata share, and only fuel, oil, airport expenditures or rental fees count.

questions.prompt: How often must you complete a flight review to act as pilot in command?
questions.why: Since the beginning of the 24th calendar month before the month of the flight; a practical test or proficiency check passed in that period also counts.

first.title: What OUPV allows
body: An OUPV endorsement lets you operate an uninspected passenger vessel of less than 100 gross register tons (GRT), with propulsion machinery of any type, carrying six or fewer passengers.

Under 100 gross tons, an uninspected passenger vessel is one carrying not more than six passengers, including at least one passenger for hire, or one chartered with the crew provided or specified by the owner and carrying not more than six passengers.

A passenger for hire is a passenger for whom consideration is contributed as a condition of carriage, whether it flows directly or indirectly to the owner, charterer, operator, agent or anyone else with an interest in the vessel.

Consideration means an economic benefit, inducement, right or profit, including payment. It does not include a voluntary sharing of the actual expenses of the voyage by money or by donating fuel, food, drink or other supplies.

The owner or the owner's representative, an individual charterer, the master, and a paid crewmember engaged in the business of the vessel who has not contributed consideration are not counted as passengers.

questions.prompt: How many passengers may an OUPV operator carry?
questions.why: OUPV covers vessels under 100 GRT carrying six or fewer passengers.

questions.prompt: What tonnage limit applies to an OUPV endorsement?
questions.why: The OUPV endorsement is for vessels of less than 100 GRT.

questions.prompt: Friends split the actual fuel and food costs of a day trip equally. Is that consideration?

questions.why: The owner and the master are excluded from the definition of passenger; a paying guest is a passenger for hire.

questions.why: For OUPV, near coastal is limited to waters not more than 100 miles offshore.

questions.why: OUPV is among the endorsements that may be granted at 18; the Coast Guard may also lower the age for OUPV applicants, with matching restrictions.

questions.why: The citizenship rule excepts operators of uninspected passenger vessels that are not documented under U.S. law.

packs.title: Locomotive Engineer and Conductor
packs.examBy: There is no single federal exam. Each railroad certifies its own engineers (49 CFR 240) and conductors (49 CFR 242) under a written certification program it files with the FRA; the program takes effect 30 days after filing unless the FRA tells the railroad it does not conform to those parts. The railroad writes and gives the knowledge test, and for engineers the skills test, on its own operating rules and territory. This pack covers the federal rules every program rests on, not any railroad's rule book.

first.title: Who needs a certificate
body: Part 240 sets minimum federal standards for the eligibility, training, testing, certification and monitoring of locomotive engineers, so that only qualified persons operate a locomotive or train. Part 242 does the same for conductors.

A locomotive engineer is anyone who moves a locomotive or group of locomotives, coupled to cars or not, whatever the job title. The exceptions are moves inside a locomotive repair or servicing area, and incidental moves of less than 100 feet for inspection or maintenance.
A conductor is the crewmember in charge of a train or yard crew. A passenger conductor is a conductor who has also had the emergency preparedness training of Part 239.

Every railroad must have a written certification program for each, and a new railroad files it with the FRA at least 60 days before it begins operations. The program takes effect 30 days after filing unless the FRA finds it does not conform. A railroad may add stricter requirements of its own, so your railroad's program and operating rules are what you are actually tested on. This pack does not cover or quote any railroad's rule book.

Parts 240 and 242 do not apply to a plant railroad that runs only on track inside an installation outside the general railroad system, to tourist or excursion operations outside that system, or to urban rapid transit not connected to it. A plant railroad moves goods only for the facility's own industrial processes; a plant that switches cars for other entities, even inside its own fence, is not one.

Running specialized roadway maintenance equipment needs no engineer certificate. A dual purpose vehicle needs none only while it is used for maintenance of way work, moves under the rules for roadway equipment, and is run by someone trained under 214.341, 214.343 and 214.355. Any other use needs an engineer who holds a Part 240 certificate.

questions.prompt: An employee moves a locomotive 60 feet on a running track purely so it can be inspected. Is that a locomotive engineer move under Part 240?
options: Yes, any move of a locomotive counts
No, it is an excepted incidental move
questions.why: Incidental moves of less than 100 feet for inspection or maintenance purposes are outside the definition of locomotive engineer.

questions.prompt: Under Part 242, who is the conductor?
options: The most senior employee on the crew
Whoever handles the radio for the crew
The crewmember in charge of the crew
The person at the locomotive controls

questions.why: Locomotive servicing engineers may operate locomotives singly or in multiple but not with cars coupled to them.

questions.prompt: How may a student engineer operate?
options: Alone, but only on yard tracks
Under an instructor engineer's direct, immediate supervision
Only with a conductor riding in the cab
questions.why: Student engineers may operate only under the direct and immediate supervision of an instructor engineer.

questions.prompt: What is the longest interval for which a railroad may certify an engineer?
questions.why: No railroad may certify a person as an engineer for an interval of more than 36 months.

questions.prompt: Which driving record entry may a railroad consider for engineer certification?
options: A DUI from five years ago
questions.why: Only impaired driving or test refusal convictions or completed state actions within 36 months count.

questions.prompt: How soon must a conductor report a DUI conviction to the employing railroad?
questions.why: Such incidents must be reported within 48 hours of the conviction or completed state action.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum horizontal field of vision in each eye?
questions.why: A field of vision of at least 70 degrees in the horizontal meridian in each eye.

questions.prompt: An engineer candidate fails the knowledge test. When may the person work as an engineer?
questions.why: No railroad may let the person function as an engineer before achieving a passing score on reexamination.

questions.prompt: Who conducts an engineer's skills performance test?
options: A Designated Supervisor of Locomotive Engineers
The train dispatcher on that territory
questions.why: The skills test is conducted by a Designated Supervisor of Locomotive Engineers.

Your training comes through your employer under the federal rules in this pack: knowing the Category B rules for the most common loads, full DOT hazmat training and testing where you handle fully regulated hazmat, and OSHA bloodborne pathogens training where your job brings occupational exposure. Some states and some clients add requirements of their own; ask them which apply to you.

first.title: Infectious substances: Category A and Category B
body: This pack covers a courier driving lab specimens, blood, medical supplies, medicines and medical waste by road. Two sets of federal rules meet in that job: the DOT Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) for what is in the package, and the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard for the person handling it. The hazmat pack covers general hazmat rules.

Division 6.2 (infectious substance) is a material known or reasonably expected to contain a pathogen: a microorganism such as a bacterium, virus, parasite or fungus, or another agent such as a prion, that can cause disease in humans or animals.

Category A is an infectious substance in a form capable of causing permanent disability or life-threatening or fatal disease in otherwise healthy humans or animals when exposure occurs. It is UN2814 (affecting humans), UN2900 (affecting animals only) or UN3549 (medical waste containing Category A, solid). Which one is assigned rests on the known medical history or symptoms of the source patient or animal, local endemic conditions, or professional judgment.

Category B is an infectious substance not in a form generally capable of causing that harm. The rule says it includes Category B substances transported for diagnostic or investigational purposes. It is described as "Biological substance, Category B" (singular, as in the Hazardous Materials Table) and is UN3373. The package marking in 173.199 uses the plural, "Biological substances, Category B".

Regulated medical waste is UN3291, not UN3373. Patient specimens are those collected directly from humans or animals for research, diagnosis, investigation, or disease treatment or prevention, including blood, tissue, swabs, excreta and specimens in transport media such as blood culture bottles. A culture is an infectious substance containing a pathogen that is intentionally propagated, and the rule says a culture does not include a patient specimen.

questions.why: Division 6.2 is a material known or reasonably expected to contain a pathogen.

questions.why: Category B is Biological substance, Category B, UN3373.

options: It is carried as a liquid rather than a solid
It travels frozen, packed in dry ice in a cooler
Its form can cause fatal or disabling disease

options: A swab from a patient with a suspected infection
Dried blood spots on filter paper
A blood tube sent to test for an infection

options: Category A, UN2814, because it is human urine
Not subject to the Division 6.2 rules
questions.why: Samples for routine testing not related to diagnosing an infectious disease, such as drug or alcohol tests, are excepted when the probability of infection is low.

options: Yes, the collector must always use one
No, not for a lab courier's hand delivery
questions.why: The shipping container is not required when a laboratory courier hand-delivers the specimens from the collection site to the laboratory.

questions.prompt: Category B triple packaging is made up of:
options: Two sealed bags inside a padded mailer
A capped tube inside an insulated cooler bag
A primary, a secondary and a rigid outer
questions.why: Category B goes in a primary receptacle, a secondary packaging and a rigid outer packaging.

questions.prompt: For a liquid Category B specimen, how much absorbent goes between the primary and the secondary?
options: None if the tube is capped tight
questions.why: The absorbent must be enough to absorb the entire contents of the primary receptacles.

questions.prompt: What goes on the outer packaging of a Category B package?
options: An INFECTIOUS SUBSTANCE label and a placard
The UN3373 diamond and the shipping name
A biohazard sticker and nothing else at all
questions.why: The UN3373 square-on-point mark is displayed with "Biological substances, Category B" next to it.

packs.examBy: There is no federal license or exam for livestock haulers or horse transporters. What the federal rules require is registration, paperwork and care standards: a carrier (a business transporting animals for hire) or an intermediate handler of animals covered by the Animal Welfare Act (such as dogs, cats, and animals used for research, exhibition or as pets) registers with USDA APHIS and files a new form every 3 years; an owner/shipper hauling horses to slaughter fills in and signs an owner-shipper certificate for each animal; and interstate livestock travels with the health and ID papers in 9 CFR 86. A CDL is needed only when the vehicle itself requires one. States, buyers and packers may add their own training or permits, such as an industry livestock handling course; ask them which apply to you.

first.title: Which federal rules reach an animal hauler
body: This pack is study preparation, not an exam. No federal agency tests animal haulers; the rules below are what USDA and FMCSA expect you to follow on the road.

Livestock in long interstate trips: the Twenty-Eight Hour Law (49 U.S.C. 80502), with USDA's statement of policy under it in 9 CFR 89. Horses and other equines hauled to slaughter: 9 CFR 88. Health papers and ID for cattle, bison, horses, poultry, sheep, goats, swine and captive cervids crossing a state line: 9 CFR 86. Moving sick animals and cleaning trucks: 9 CFR 71.

Dogs, cats, primates, rabbits and other warmblooded animals used or meant for research, teaching, testing, experimentation, exhibition or as pets: the Animal Welfare Act rules in 9 CFR 1, 2 and 3. Under 9 CFR 1.1, "animal" for those rules excludes horses not used for research and farm animals such as livestock or poultry used for food or fiber, so a cattle or hog hauler is not an AWA carrier for those loads.

An AWA carrier is the operator of an airline, railroad, motor carrier, shipping line or other enterprise in the business of transporting any animals for hire. An intermediate handler is a business that receives custody of animals in connection with their transport in commerce and is not a dealer, research facility, exhibitor, auction operator or carrier. A pet owner driving their own dog is neither: the carrier definition needs a business of transporting animals for hire, and the intermediate handler definition a business that takes custody of animals for their transport.

Hours of service: FMCSA's livestock exemption is in 49 CFR 395.1(k). The CDL itself has no livestock endorsement; whether you need a CDL depends on the vehicle, as in the CDL General Knowledge pack. States may add rules of their own on top of all of these; check yours.

For dogs, the 9 CFR 1.1 definition of "animal" means all dogs, including those used for hunting, security or breeding, so a business hauling working dogs for hire is an AWA carrier just as it is for pets. The same section counts horses and llamas used solely as work and pack animals as farm animals, and "animal" excludes horses not used for research and other farm animals.

questions.prompt: Under the Twenty-Eight Hour Law, animals may be confined in a vehicle without unloading for feed, water and rest for no more than:
questions.why: The statute sets 28 consecutive hours, unless one of its exceptions applies (sheep at night, unavoidable causes, or 36 hours on the owner's written request).

questions.prompt: How can the 28 hour period be extended to 36 hours?
options: The driver takes a 10 hour off duty break on the way
The owner asks in writing, apart from the bill of lading
The trip stays under 500 miles from origin to destination
questions.why: The owner or person having custody must ask in writing, separate from the bill of lading or other rail form.

questions.prompt: Under Part 89, livestock delayed en route so their confinement materially exceeds the Twenty-Eight Hour Law's limit should get:
options: Extra feed in proportion to the excess time
No feed until they reach the destination
Water only, with no extra feed at all
questions.why: Part 89 says that when a delay makes confinement materially exceed the law's period, the livestock should get additional feed in proportion to the excess time.

questions.prompt: Livestock held at a feeding station 12 hours after their last feed was substantially eaten should be fed again, unless the hold plus the time to the next station or destination would not ordinarily exceed:
questions.why: Part 89 lets them be held longer without that feeding if the hold plus the time to the next feeding station or destination, whichever is closer, would not ordinarily exceed 40 hours.

questions.prompt: Part 89 says livestock should be unloaded into pens for feed, water and rest unless:
options: The weather on the route stays mild
All can lie down at once in the car
The driver is still within hours
questions.why: Unloading is called for unless there is ample room in the car for all of the animals to lie down at the same time.

questions.prompt: When hogs are watered in the vehicle, water should be available for not less than:
questions.why: In the case of hogs, water should be available for not less than 1 hour.

questions.prompt: Can equines for slaughter ride in a trailer with two stacked decks?
options: Yes, if each deck has enough headroom
No, they ride on one level only
Yes, for ponies and donkeys only
questions.why: Equines for slaughter may not ride in a cargo space with two or more stacked levels; the 2006 allowance has ended and floating decks must be set to one level.

questions.prompt: Under Part 88, who is an owner/shipper?
options: Anyone who hauls a single horse to a sale barn
The slaughter plant that buys the horses
One who hauls over 20 a year to slaughter
questions.why: An owner/shipper commercially transports more than 20 equines a year to slaughter, unless it is incidental to producing food or fiber.

questions.prompt: On a slaughter load, each stallion and each aggressive equine must be:
options: Tied short at the front of the trailer
Loaded last, nearest the rear door
questions.why: Each stallion and any aggressive equine is completely segregated so it cannot contact any other equine.

questions.prompt: Before loading for slaughter, each equine gets food, water and rest for at least:
questions.why: The owner/shipper provides food, potable water and rest for not less than 6 consecutive hours immediately before loading.

first.title: When an armored truck is a commercial motor vehicle
body: No federal agency licenses armored car drivers, messengers or guards as such. What the federal rules do reach is the truck: if it is a commercial motor vehicle, the driver and the carrier follow the federal motor carrier safety rules. Guard licensing and the right to carry a weapon come from the state, covered at the end of this pack.

Under the federal safety rules, a vehicle used on a highway in interstate commerce to transport property is a commercial motor vehicle if its gross vehicle weight rating or gross combination weight rating, or its gross vehicle weight or gross combination weight, is 10,001 pounds (4,536 kg) or more, whichever is greater. The other tests are passenger seating and placarded hazardous materials.
So check both your truck's GVWR and its loaded weight. This pack does not assume a typical figure: the numbers for your own vehicle decide.

Interstate commerce means trade, traffic or transportation between a place in a state and a place outside it, between two places in a state through another state or a place outside the United States, or between two places in a state as part of a movement that begins or ends outside the state or the country. Anything else is intrastate commerce. Your state sets the rules for it, and they may differ from the federal ones, so ask your state.

A motor carrier is a for-hire motor carrier or a private motor carrier. A for-hire motor carrier is a person engaged in the transportation of goods or passengers for compensation; a private motor carrier transports property or passengers by commercial motor vehicle and is not for-hire. A company paid to carry other businesses' cash is transporting goods for compensation, so it fits the for-hire definition.

questions.prompt: An armored truck has a GVWR of 14,000 pounds and runs a route across a state line. Is it a commercial motor vehicle under the federal safety rules?
options: No, since it carries no passengers
questions.why: A property vehicle in interstate commerce rated or weighing 10,001 pounds or more is a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.prompt: A truck is rated at 9,800 pounds but weighs 10,400 pounds loaded on an interstate run. Which figure decides whether it is a commercial motor vehicle?
questions.why: The definition uses the rating or the actual weight, whichever is greater.

questions.prompt: A route runs between two branches in one state but passes through a neighboring state on the way. What kind of commerce is it?
options: Neither, since both ends are in one state
questions.why: Transportation between two places in a state through another state is interstate commerce.

questions.prompt: An armored car company carries other businesses' cash for a fee. What kind of motor carrier is it?
options: Not a motor carrier, since it is a security firm
questions.why: A for-hire motor carrier is engaged in transporting goods or passengers for compensation, and cash carried for a fee is goods carried for pay.

questions.prompt: A straight armored truck has a GVWR of 22,000 pounds, weighs under 26,001 pounds loaded, tows nothing, carries no placarded hazmat and is not built for 16 passengers. Does the driver need a CDL under the federal rule?
questions.why: It meets none of the Group A, B or C definitions, so no CDL is needed federally.

questions.prompt: At what GVWR does a single vehicle become Group B?
questions.why: Group B is a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more.

questions.prompt: Do the federal CDL rules in part 383 reach a driver whose routes never leave the state?
options: No, part 383 reaches interstate drivers only
Yes, they cover intrastate commerce too
questions.why: Part 383 applies to commercial motor vehicle drivers in interstate, foreign or intrastate commerce.

questions.prompt: What is a vehicle's gross vehicle weight rating?
options: The scale weight on the day of the trip
The carrier's estimate of the heaviest load
questions.why: GVWR is the value the manufacturer specifies as the loaded weight of a single vehicle.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum age to drive a commercial motor vehicle under the federal driver qualification rule?
questions.why: A qualified driver is at least 21 years old.

questions.prompt: You drive a 15,000-pound armored truck interstate and hold no CDL. Where must your medical examiner's certificate be while you are on duty?
options: On your person, the original or a copy
With the carrier's driver file at the terminal
questions.why: A driver without a CDL carries the original or a copy of a current certificate when on duty.

first.title: IS-100: What ICS is and who commands
body: This pack is study preparation, not the exam. FEMA's Independent Study Program gives the real final exam for each course; this pack does not copy those exams.

The Incident Command System (ICS) is a standardized approach to the command, control and coordination of on-scene incident management. It is used by all levels of government and by many NGOs and private sector organizations. NIMS applies to all incidents, from traffic accidents to major disasters, and using ICS on every incident keeps the skills sharp.

ICS has five major functional areas, staffed as needed: Command, Operations, Planning, Logistics and Finance/Administration. A sixth function, Intelligence/Investigations, is used only when an incident needs it, and the Incident Commander decides where it sits: in the Planning Section, in the Operations Section, on the Command Staff, as its own General Staff section, or a mix of these.

The Incident Commander is responsible for on-scene incident activities, including developing incident objectives and ordering and releasing resources. The Command Staff report directly to the Incident Commander: the Public Information Officer (PIO), who handles information for the public, media and other agencies; the Safety Officer, who monitors operations, advises command on the health and safety of incident personnel, and stops or prevents unsafe acts; and the Liaison Officer, the point of contact for agencies and organizations not in the command.
The Incident Commander or Unified Command approves the release of incident information. When several agencies have PIOs, one is designated the lead PIO.
FEMA's NIMS Training Program lists IS-100 and IS-700 for all personnel working in ICS, and adds IS-200 and IS-800 for those with leadership responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which list names the five major ICS functional areas?
options: Command, Operations, Dispatch, Logistics, Public Information
questions.why: Command, Operations, Planning, Logistics and Finance/Administration, staffed as needed.

questions.prompt: Which position is NOT part of the Command Staff?
questions.why: The Planning Section Chief is General Staff; the Command Staff are the PIO, Safety Officer and Liaison Officer.

questions.prompt: Who may alter, suspend or stop an activity that is immediately dangerous to the life and health of personnel?
questions.why: The Safety Officer alters, suspends or terminates activities immediately dangerous to life and health.

questions.prompt: Which two courses does FEMA's NIMS Training Program list for all personnel working in ICS?
questions.why: IS-100 and IS-700 for all ICS personnel; IS-200 and IS-800 are added for leadership responsibilities.

questions.prompt: What is the title of the person who leads a Branch?
questions.why: Branches are led by Directors; divisions and groups by Supervisors; sections by Chiefs.

questions.prompt: How do divisions and groups differ?
options: Divisions are functional; groups are geographic
Both are geographic, but groups are smaller
Divisions are geographic; groups are functional
questions.why: Divisions always refer to geographic assignments and groups always refer to functional ones.

questions.prompt: Five dump trucks of the same kind and type working under one leader form a:
questions.why: A strike team is a set number of resources of the same kind and type under a designated leader.

questions.prompt: No Logistics Section Chief has been assigned yet. Who is responsible for logistics?
questions.why: General Staff functions default to the Incident Commander or Unified Command until a section chief is assigned.

questions.prompt: Before an incoming team takes over a county's flood response, the county administrator gives its Incident Commander a written statement of the commander's responsibilities, priorities and limits. What is that document?
questions.why: A delegation of authority is the statement from the jurisdiction that assigns the Incident Commander specific responsibilities and authorities, typically with priorities, expectations and constraints.

questions.prompt: Under NIMS, what does the transfer of command process include?
options: A briefing, and notice to all personnel
Approval from the state EOC director
A new written IAP signed by both commanders
questions.why: The transfer includes a briefing that captures essential information and notifying all personnel involved in the incident.
